summary: Live Optimize console walkthrough focused on choosing precision profiles (INT8 vs FP8) for Cobalt Labs' inference workloads. Demonstrated sandbox runs, showed quality regressions on edge prompts, walked through fallback policies and canary rollout approach. Agreed to provide sandbox + benchmark artifacts and schedule POC scoping.
topics: precision profiles, INT8 vs FP8, fallback rules, canary rollouts, latency SLOs, quality delta measurement, qprofile sandbox, KV cache/prefix caching, cost per token tradeoffs, security considerations (KMS, data residency)
transcript:
[00:00] Sam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick roll call? um let's get names.
[00:08] Ellen (Cobalt): Ellen Park here. Head of ML.
[00:11] Jason (Cobalt): Jason Reed, platform.
[00:13] Maya (Cobalt): Maya Ortiz, product.
[00:16] Lina (Redwood SE): Lina Gomez, systems and Optimize lead. Marcus and Priya silently wave.
[00:22] Sam: Cool. Goal for today is hands-on through the Optimize console qprofile flow, show INT8 vs FP8 tradeoffs, and map that to your latency SLO and quality thresholds. we'll keep it practical.
[00:34] Ellen: Great, we shipped a prototype last quarter, 95th p99 latency matters, and we have some hallucination sensitivity on clinical prompts, so quality is a blocker.
[00:44] Jason: also need to confirm this can run in our VPC / private deployment eventually. security questions later.
[00:49] Lina: noted. we'll point out where Private and Dedicated change choices. quick context: what model family are you using?
[00:55] Ellen: Open-source medium-sized LLM, cust-model v3, roughly 8k context in our tests, typical prompt length 60 tokens, responses ~220 tokens.
[01:05] Marcus: ok, good to know. so token distribution skews right, longer outputs, so FP8 tends to preserve quality at larger decode lengths, INT8 may drop fidelity especially on rare token choices.
[01:18] Sam: i'm going to share my screen — opening Optimize console, sandbox project for Cobalt. link posted: https://redwood.example/sandbox/cobalt-qprofile (shared).
[01:28] [screen share noises]
[01:30] Lina: first demo, we ran an INT8 qprofile to cut cost ~38% vs FP8 on this workload. baseline FP8 latency 90ms p95, INT8 dropped to 62ms p95; quality delta measured on your eval set: average BLEU-ish metric down ~3.7%, but a subset of clinical prompts fell much more.
[01:51] Ellen: ok that's the risk we saw. can you show the failing prompts?
[01:54] Lina: yep. navigating to Optimize -> Sensitivity -> Heatmap. here's a few examples: prompt ID CLN-14 returns missing critical token in INT8 run, spelled as 'patient' vs 'patent' (transcription: "patent" sometimes shows incorrectly), so small token probs shift.
[02:16] Jason: ouch. pipeline uses strict downstream extractor, so token changes break fields.
[02:22] Sam: this is why we recommend hybrid policies — keep FP8 for critical paths, INT8 for other routes. we'll show configuring route-aware qprofiles.
[02:31] [00:02:40] Lina: creating a canary: route = /extract, precision fallback FP8 forced for steps where named-entity recall >= threshold. we can do prefix-based caching to reduce tokens on repeated calls too — KV cache (note: transcribed earlier as KV cash in some runs).
[02:49] Maya: can you explain the cost math again?
[02:52] Marcus: sure. simplified: FP8 run cost per token X, INT8 is about 0.62X on the same GPU due to smaller memory bandwidth and packing. but throughput and batching interplay; if you can batch, INT8 sometimes gets closer to FP8 latency per token.
[03:12] [00:03:20] Lina: here's the Q-profile editor: you can set sample workloads, run quick sensitivity sweep (5 warmup runs + 20 samples), it will auto-generate candidate profiles sorted by quality drop and latency gain.
[03:30] Ellen: how reliable are the auto-suggestions? we've seen ML systems optimize for average rather than tail cases.
[03:36] Lina: good point. the suggestions include a "fidelity lane" flag — we compute a per-prompt delta and highlight prompts with >2x regression. You can tag a prompt as 'must preserve' and that will force FP8 path via routing.
[03:51] Sam: also we keep audit traces for each decision in the Console, full diffs for outputs between profiles; good for compliance and post-mortem.
[03:59] Jason: about private deployment — will qprofiles run the same?
[04:03] Lina: yes. the runtime selection logic is consistent across Hosted/Dedicated/Private. kernel selection differs slightly by HW but profile semantics are same. in on-prem we surface the same optimizer but with limited telemetry by default.
[04:18] [00:04:30] Maya: show me a real side-by-side.
[04:33] Lina: switching to compare view. FP8 output first, then INT8. look at sample CLN-07: FP8 -> "does not indicate active TB"; INT8 -> "no signs of TB" — subtle but downstream classifier mislabels severity.
[04:52] Ellen: that's exactly the issue. That nuance drives triage.
[04:56] Sam: two operational patterns we recommend: 1) Canary with shadowing: run INT8 in shadow, route only to FP8 until quality gates pass. 2) Route-based: annotate endpoints where you can't accept degradation. Both can be combined with automatic fallback.
[05:12] Lina: demoing fallback policy: create policy, set metric = recall_on_key_entities >= 0.98, action = switch to FP8 on failure for next N requests, and post a notification to slack.
[05:27] [00:05:40] Marcus: note on batching — if your front end aggregates short prompts into micro-batches, INT8's throughput improvements amplify. but if you have high variance length, caching prefix helps more.
[05:40] Jason: any gotchas on KV cache and privacy? we can't store PII in cache unencrypted.
[05:45] Lina: can enable per-tenant cache encryption using your KMS and set TTLs. for Private deployments you can keep cache nodes in customer VPC and logs minimal.
[05:58] Sam: transcribed note — customer requested security docs. we'll send SOC2/ISO attestation plus KMS integration guide. (action item).
[06:06] [00:06:20] Ellen: about evaluation metrics — we track both automatic and human evaluation. human-in-loop for edge cases?
[06:12] Lina: yes, Optimize has an eval batch export that you can push to your annotators; we link to the diff artifacts for each candidate profile. you can store annotations against prompt IDs.
[06:24] Maya: how long does a sensitivity sweep take?
[06:26] Lina: typical for your dataset (2k eval prompts) with warmups on hosted sandbox ~30-45 minutes for a full sweep across the main candidates. a quick sweep subset is 10-15 minutes. depends on sequence lengths.
[06:40] [00:06:50] Sam: let's run a quick 20-sample sweep now on CLN sample set so you can see the UI. starting now. (runs).
[07:00] [00:07:10] [system noise] Sweep complete: shows distribution chart. INT8 median latency ~60ms, FP8 ~88ms. Quality scatter shows cluster of 4 prompts with >6% drop.
[07:26] Ellen: can we export the examples that fail?
[07:28] Lina: yes — export CSV or attach to JIRA ticket. exporting. link: https://redwood.example/artifacts/ff-20250729-cln-failures.csv
[07:38] Jason: good. we'll push those to our annotators.
[07:42] [00:07:50] Maya: on the sandbox, can we test this with our auth and SSO?
[07:47] Sam: sandbox supports SAML test connector; i'll include instructions in the invite.
[07:52] Lina: quick note: when you move to Dedicated with reserved GPU pools, the latency curves compress and INT8 improvements may shrink a bit because kernel choices on that hardware are different. but cost savings still generally hold.
[08:08] Ellen: what about rollout and rollback automation?
[08:11] Lina: console supports automatic rollback if quality gates fail post-rollout; you can define evaluation windows and min-sample counts.
[08:20] Sam: Jon from infra asked offline about whether the qprofile artifacts are portable — yes, we version-lock profiles and you can export/import JSON objects.
[08:30] [00:08:40] Jason: team asked about observability — token-level cost, per-route latency breakdown?
[08:34] Marcus: yes detailed, we show per-token time breakdown, batching stats, KV cache hit rates, and cost estimations by route.
[08:42] [00:08:50] Ellen: can you show how we set the 'must preserve' prompts?
[08:55] Lina: clicking "Tag prompts" -> select CLN-07, CLN-14 -> set preserve=true -> policies auto-generate routes that send those prompt signatures to FP8. done. check.
[09:08] Maya: curious about mixed precision — can the runtime do internal mixed-precision on same seq?
[09:13] Marcus: runtime supports per-layer kernel choices for advanced setups, but qprofiles in console are easiest to reason about. mixed-per-layer needs validation. we'll surface that as an advanced lab.
[09:25] [00:09:35] Sam: let's go through expected deliverables: we'll give you sandbox, a sample evaluation run with INT8/FP8 comparisons, and a short doc on routing and fallback. anything else?
[09:41] Ellen: security docs and a cost estimate for 1M tokens/month please.
[09:45] Sam: noted.
[09:47] [00:09:55] Maya: timeline: target POC decision in 3 weeks.
[09:51] Sam: we'll aim to have artifacts by next week and schedule scoping Aug 5.
[09:56] [00:10:05] Lina: quick Q/A time — Jason asked "what about competitor lock-in?"
[10:01] Jason (Cobalt): yeah, if we rely on Redwood-specific qprofile semantics would that lock us?
[10:06] Lina: profiles are exported as JSON with clear rules; you can re-run sweeps in other runtimes but kernel behavior may differ. so it's not vendor-locking on intent, but numerical behavior can vary.
[10:18] Ellen: are there any caveats with hallucination metrics? we use F1 on entities and a custom severity score.
[10:24] Marcus: we support custom metrics; you can upload your scoring function as a lambda that runs inside the sandbox eval harness (runs with restricted resources). we'll provide an example.
[10:36] [00:10:45] Sam: wrapping up — recap of next steps and action items to owners. i'll drop links and timeline into the CRM.
[10:45] Maya: sounds good. thanks team.
[10:48] [00:10:58] Sam: thanks everyone. end call.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, model name sometimes rendered as "cust-model v3" when recorded). Shared artifacts: sandbox link, failure CSV, qprofile template, SOC2 doc (links provided in follow-up).

Action items (in-line): Sam to send sandbox invite; Lina to export benchmark run; Jason to provide token distribution and SLO.

Recap/Next steps: 1) Redwood to provision sandbox + SAML test connector and share qprofile template. 2) Cobalt to annotate failing prompts and return POC acceptance criteria. 3) Schedule Aug 5 POC scoping.
final_recap: Provision sandbox + sample runs, send security docs, schedule POC scoping on Aug 5. Owners: Sam (sandbox + docs), Lina (bench exports), Jason (SLO & token dist).
